title: Family of Kamloops shooting victim want Mounties to answer questions
article: Family members of a man shot dead by Kamloops police want some answers.
Stephen Hanaghan, 45, of Kamloops died Monday after he rammed a stolen red and white pickup truck into a police car. An RCMP officer, who had just exited the car, shot him.
Police said Hanaghan reversed into the officer's SUV and pushed it back about three metres, leading the policeman to fear for his life.
"No one knows what happened yet, except for the police," said Hanaghan's sister Claire. "Was the cop in a direct line with his vehicle? Was he at risk? Or was it just an adrenaline reaction?"
Kamloops RCMP Cpl. Fran Bethell said the policeman shot Hanaghan because he feared he'd be killed.
"The actions of the suspect dictate the police response," Bethell said.
The shooting will dealt with during a coroner's inquest, Bethell said.
Hanaghan, with a passenger, was fleeing the RCMP after an attempted break-in at a gas station around 5 a.m., police said.

Hanaghan was to appear today in Kamloops Provincial Court on a theft-under-$5,000 charge from an incident last month. He'd also been charged with possession of stolen property and possession of a firearm without a licence.
Hanaghan's passenger, a 45-year-old man from Kamloops, was arrested and later released without charges.
Police continue investigating the break-in attempt at the gas station and anticipate laying charges.
